audience: people with more than one account, bill or income source who want them in one real place, not five apps (shop listing, audience)
the person rebuilding a financial binder or money binder for the end-of-year check, who pins printable section pages and tracker sheets
someone who keeps getting charged for subscriptions they forgot about and wants a list with renewal dates (shop listing, searchedProblems)
couples and roommates who split rent and utilities and can't remember what was squared up last time
people who download a bank statement CSV rather than link their bank, and want it turned into a usable list
planners who save sinking fund trackers, variable-bill worksheets and 'what a normal month costs' pages
people sorting their money out after a move, a job change or a breakup (shop listing, searchedProblems)

visualWorld.setting: A private desk where someone keeps their whole financial life in order: an open three-ring financial binder with numbered index tabs, the 81-page Printable Finance Companion workbook pages beside it, a pencil, and a phone that shows the live app. It is the archive of a whole financial life, area by area (accounts, income, bills, subscriptions, transactions, debt, savings), and not one month's envelope. That keeps it separate from Monthly Money Reset, whose world is this month's safe-to-spend number. The product's own identity motif is literally 'index' (src/products/personal-finance-companion/definition.ts, theme.identity.motif), so tabs, registers and labelled rows are its natural language.

Seven index tabs stick out of the right edge, stepped down, each a rounded-top rect in a tint of the accent scale with a two-digit number and short section name.

Divider tabs on their own: rounded-top rects 120x56, stacked with 8px overlap, numbered 01 to 07 or 01 to 10 in Newsreader, labels in IBM Plex Sans caps. The active tab is solid accent with white text; the others are soft #dbe8e2 with ink text.

Portrait paper rect (#fafbf9) at 8.5:11 ratio with a 3.5px accent bar across the top (the 'spine' the real workbook and Money Book print), a small running head in caps, an eyebrow in accent caps, a Newsreader title, a 1.2px ink rule under it, ruled write lines (#c8d6cd), and a folio number bottom right. Copy the real page's eyebrow and title exactly.

Five to six workbook-pages fanned from a shared pivot below the frame, rotated -14, -7, 0, 7, 14 degrees. Each has a flat offset shadow (same rect, 8px down-right, ink at 8% opacity), and its real title is readable on the top page and the two pages either side.

One workbook-page shown large, tilted 3 to 4 degrees, with a table: an ink 1px header rule, header labels in small caps, 5 to 12 rows of #c8d6cd lines. Entries are set in IBM Plex Sans in a body-ink colour so they read as written in, with tabular figures. A pencil lies across one corner.
Long hexagonal pencil: butter-yellow body rect with two faint facet lines, a pink eraser cap, a thin metal ferrule band, a wood cone triangle and a graphite tip triangle.

Five rounded pill stamps with a 2px outline and caps text: CONFIRMED (accent fill, white text), ESTIMATED (soft fill), UNRESOLVED (outline only), MISSING (dashed outline), STALE (faint grey). These are the workbook's real labels; place them next to rows like stamps, slightly rotated.

A torn-edge paper strip or plain text panel in a monospace face: a header line and raw comma-separated rows, quotes visible around '"1,612.40"', minus signs visible. Zigzag polygon on the bottom edge for the tear.

A rounded white card (radius 20) with three header chips (Date, Description, Amount) in soft-accent pills, ruled rows, amounts right-aligned in tabular figures, and one row tinted amber with a small flag shape to mark a likely duplicate.
Two or three curved accent arrows (quadratic bezier path, 4px stroke, round caps, small triangular head) running from raw header words on the csv-strip to the header chips on the tidy-table.

Five small flat objects in a row or loose pile: a thought bubble (circle plus two small circles), a speech or sticky-note square with three lines, a .txt file (rect with a folded corner triangle), a spreadsheet sheet (rect with a 3x4 grid), and a ticked checklist. One per real starting option in OrientationStep.tsx.

An app-style record card: white rounded rect with a 1px border (#e5e8e6), a name in semibold, a small status pill (e.g. 'Annual' badge or 'Ready'), the amount right-aligned, a secondary line in muted grey. Shown big, as if lifted out of the app.
The app's own date leaf from TodayView.tsx: a 42x46 rounded rect with a coloured band on top holding a three-letter month in caps and the day number large below. Scale it up 4 to 6 times.

One large card in front: wash background (#eef4f1), a 6px accent bar on the left edge (the Money Book 'box' style), one sentence in Newsreader, and a small accent arrow chip. Behind it, faded to 25% opacity, a wall of 12 to 16 blank sticky squares at random small angles, with grey lines only and no words.
The app's paid/settled control: a 2px circle; when ticked, an accent-filled circle with a white check path. Draw one empty and one ticked side by side when contrast helps.

A thick rounded horizontal bar for one shared bill, split into two segments by share (e.g. 67 and 33) in accent and soft accent, with a person glyph at each end (circle head and rounded-shoulder arc). Each segment carries its amount.

A one-page sheet titled 'Shared Responsibility' in a serif, a muted 'As of' line, two short lists (settled lines with a tick, still-owed lines without), and a ruled 'Total owed to you' row in bold. A paper-plane or envelope outline sits beside it for 'send'.

Mason jars: a rounded-rect glass body with 10% ink outline, a lid band rect with a thread line, an accent fill rect clipped to the body to show how full it is, and a small paper label rect with the fund name and monthly amount. Labels only ever carry a real example from the sinking funds guide.

A horizontal track with a shaded band between a low cap and a high cap, a small tick marked 'midpoint', and the low and high amounts written under the caps. It reads as a thermometer laid on its side, without the bulb.

The workbook's payoff ladder (page 38): a ladder of five rungs numbered 1 at the bottom to 5 at the top, side rails as two tall rounded rects, the lower rungs filled accent ('shaded as cleared') and the upper ones outline only.

One long rounded bar split into three segments, as on the app's MonthCard (TodayView.tsx): Going out (dark ink tint), Set aside for goals (mid tint), Left over (accent), with labels under each segment and 'coming in' written above the whole bar.
An index card (rounded rect at a 5:3 ratio, with a faint ruled-line texture and a punched hole circle top left) titled 'Quick reference card' and six numbered lines, numbers in accent Newsreader.

A row of 15 small day squares from a heads-up date to a renewal date. The first square is outlined in accent ('heads-up'), the last is filled accent with the calendar-leaf on top ('renews'), and a bracket underneath says '14 days'.
Three pill toggles in a row: Keep, Still deciding, Planned to cancel. One is selected (accent fill); the others are outlined. No scissors or cancel icons, because the product never cancels anything.

The existing Phone frame (creative/src/visual/Phone) holding one real screenshot from creative/public/screens/personal-finance-companion-*.png (bills, debt, printables, records). It is used small and to one side so the drawn prop stays the hero.

A messy pile of 4 to 6 rects at random angles: a statement with ruled lines, a receipt with a zigzag bottom edge, a sticky note, and two rounded-rect app tiles with a single generic bank glyph (columns and pediment). They are grey-toned so the tidy result stands out.

visualWorld.palette: Built from the product's own accent scale (definition.ts theme.accentScale): forest/ink #0d3b2e as the one strong colour, strong #08281f for headline ink on light grounds, soft #dbe8e2 and wash #eef4f1 for tabs and cards. Paper and rules come from the Money Book (printables/moneyBook.tsx): paper #fafbf9, ink #161d1a, body #333c37, rule #dde5e0, write lines #c8d6cd. One warm pop only, the pink popFor() already returns for this accent (hsl(340 80% 80%)) or a butter yellow for the pencil, used for at most one highlight per pin (a highlighted renewal date, an active tab). Amber is reserved for the real 'needs a look' or duplicate flag. Dark-hero pins may use the app's hero gradient #256049 to #0d3b2e with white type. Type matches the workbook: Newsreader for headlines and page titles, IBM Plex Sans for labels and table text, Fraunces only for a single figure where the figure is the point.
visualWorld.mood: Quiet, orderly and private: the feeling of a well-kept binder on a Sunday evening. Paper texture and ruled lines, generous margins, nothing shouting. It should feel competent and calm, never 'get rich' or hustle. Gaps are shown honestly (Missing, a question mark, a dashed outline) because the product treats a known gap as useful.

archetypes.name: The tabbed financial binder
archetypes.clicks: Money binders and budget binders are an established printable genre on Pinterest and Etsy, with sellers still publishing yearly binder sets (e.g. a free 2026 budget binder). Section-by-section binder pins answer 'what goes in it', which is a save-for-later question. Search interest for 'budget binder' itself is reported as softening, so this archetype leads with the sections and the binder is the frame.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-330: headline in Newsreader, 2-3 lines, left-aligned at x=72, with an optional small caps tag above it. 330-1230: the open financial-binder drawn about 860 wide, centred and tilted -3 degrees, with its seven index tabs on the right edge each carrying a real section name; the open page shows one section's real content (or, on product pins, a phone-screenshot clipped into the page as if the page were the app). 1250-1340: one sub line. 1360-1460: product line (name, 'Made by Draftpace', price or 'Free guide'), kept clear of the bottom-right corner where Pinterest UI sits.
archetypes.visual: Open three-ring binder with numbered index tabs; the open page is a workbook-page or the live Records screen.
archetypes.text: Tab labels are real section names: the binder guide's seven (src/content/guides.ts financial-binder-what-to-include, timeline 'The seven sections, in the order to fill them') or the workbook's (Printable Finance Companion PDF, section dividers 01-10). The page content is copied from the guide's example tables or the workbook's real page headings.
archetypes.bestFor: financial binder, 'what goes in', 'all in one place', seven areas, section-by-section explainers

archetypes.name: What's inside the 81-page workbook
archetypes.clicks: Printable sellers are advised to show several images of the actual pages rather than one cover, and pin designers report that collage-style pins showing several pages or steps in one 2:3 frame earn saves. A fanned stack of real, named pages is the 'what's inside' pin that printable buyers expect, and it proves the product exists.
archetypes.layout: Top 0-300: headline. 300-1100: workbook-fan of 5-6 real pages fanned from a pivot below centre, about 820 wide, with the top page's title legible at about 30px. 1100-1250: three fact chips in a row (e.g. '81 pages', 'US Letter and A4', 'Twelve monthly reviews'). 1250-1330: sub line. 1360-1460: product line. Optionally a phone-screenshot (printables screen) overlapping the lower right of the fan at 30% of the width.
archetypes.visual: Fanned pages of the real Printable Finance Companion workbook, each with its real eyebrow and title.
archetypes.text: Page titles copied from the workbook PDF (src/products/personal-finance-companion/printables/printableFinanceCompanionLetter.base64.ts, decoded: 81 pages; e.g. 'Subscription inventory' p26, 'Variable bills worksheet' p22, 'Debt payoff method comparison' p38, 'Sinking funds worksheet' p42, 'Net worth snapshot' p46, 'January: review' p54). Fact chips come from the binder guide's closing paragraph ('81-page form, in US Letter and A4', 'twelve monthly review spreads').
archetypes.bestFor: the workbook itself, paper-plus-app pins, 'what you get' pins, gentle-start pins that show the workbook's gap pages

archetypes.name: One tracker sheet, filled in
archetypes.clicks: Tracker and log printables (savings trackers, sinking fund trackers, bill logs) are among the most common money printables, and budget trackers are among the best-selling Etsy printable categories. Checklists, templates and filled examples are the save-for-later formats. A sheet filled with a believable example row set shows exactly how to use it.
archetypes.layout: Top 0-300: headline. 300-1180: one tracker-sheet about 820 wide, tilted 3 degrees, with a real column header row and 4-12 filled rows. A pencil crosses the lower-left corner, and one cell is highlighted with the pop colour (the field the pin is about). 1200-1320: sub line. 1360-1460: product line or 'Free guide'.
archetypes.visual: A workbook-style register page with real column headers and example entries written in.
archetypes.text: Column headers come from the workbook page or guide table the pin is about. Row entries come only from that guide's own 'Example only' tables, never invented. Each pin's content.source names the table.
archetypes.bestFor: subscription tracker, variable bills, sinking funds worksheet, accounts page with confidence labels, shared statement, one-page monthly budget, CSV check sheet

archetypes.name: Statement in, tidy table out
archetypes.clicks: Before-and-after pins are listed among the formats that get saved, and 'turn X into Y' is the shape of the CSV, notes and scattered-finances pins. A transformation shown in one frame (raw text on one side, clean rows on the other) explains the product in a glance, with no promise of bank linking.
archetypes.layout: Top 0-280: headline. 280-640: the 'before' (csv-strip, loose-papers or source-objects), slightly grey and tilted. 640-760: mapping-arrows or one bold down-arrow in accent. 760-1200: the 'after' (tidy-table, or a phone-screenshot of the Records screen), crisp and straight. 1210-1320: sub line. 1360-1460: product line.
archetypes.visual: Raw CSV text, pasted notes or a pile of scattered sources becoming one clean, reviewed table.
archetypes.text: Raw rows are the CSV guide's four example rows (bank-statement-csv-to-budget, the Date/Description/Amount table). Header chips are the app's real mapping labels (CsvImportFlow.tsx: 'Description column', 'Separate Debit / Credit columns'). Source labels are the real Companion options (OrientationStep.tsx). The review note is real copy ('Nothing from an import joins your picture until you confirm it.', TodayView.tsx).
archetypes.bestFor: bank statement CSV, budgeting from statements, scattered finances, 'from a pile of tabs to one picture', importing notes

archetypes.name: Two sides of one bill (or one choice)
archetypes.clicks: Comparison and 'which is better' charts are a staple money-pin format, and the couples niche is built around comparing split methods (equal versus income-based versus by item). A side-by-side answers a decision in one look and invites a save to 'show my partner'.
archetypes.layout: Top 0-300: headline. 300-1150: the frame divided into two columns (or one split-bar across the width with a person glyph at each end); each side has a header in caps and 2-4 short lines, with a settled-tick or shared-statement where relevant. 1170-1320: sub line. 1360-1460: product line.
archetypes.visual: A shared bill split into your share and their share, a settled tick, the one-page Shared Responsibility statement; or snowball and avalanche as two columns.
archetypes.text: Split numbers are the split-bills guide's own example ($4,200 and $2,100 take-home, 67/33, Rent $1,800 to $1,200.00 and $600.00). The methods table is from the same guide. Snowball and avalanche results are from the debt-snowball-vs-avalanche guide's worked example. Statement wording is from generateSharedStatement.tsx ('Shared Responsibility', 'Total owed to you').
archetypes.bestFor: couples and roommates splitting bills, settled versus owed, snowball versus avalanche

archetypes.name: One card, not a to-do wall
archetypes.clicks: Pinterest's own guidance is to keep one clear focal subject with short, legible overlay text. A single oversized card against a faded wall of blank notes is the strongest single image for the product's core promise of one next move, and it works as a 'how it works' pin for one record (a subscription, a goal, a quick reference card).
archetypes.layout: Top 0-300: headline. 330-1150: one card about 780x520 to 780x700, centred and straight, with a soft shadow; behind it either the faded sticky wall (next-move pins) or nothing but paper texture. Small numbered callouts (1, 2, 3) may point at fields on the card. 1170-1320: sub line. 1360-1460: product line.
archetypes.visual: One big card: a next-move message, one subscription record, one savings goal, one shared bill row, or the workbook's quick reference card.
archetypes.text: Card copy uses the app's real message templates (attention.ts, e.g. '${bill.name} needs a due date.'; TodayView.tsx 'You're caught up.'), filled with names and figures from the guides' own examples; or real field labels (SubscriptionFormSheet.tsx, CandidateReviewQueue.tsx); or the workbook quick reference card (PDF p79).
archetypes.bestFor: one next move, the Attention inbox, renewal date, goal monthly amount, a shared row, the ten-minute starting path, importing notes, CSV mapping

archetypes.name: Jars, ranges and ladders
archetypes.clicks: Visual progress trackers you colour in or fill (sinking fund envelope trackers, savings charts, 'colour a heart when you save') are among the most common money printables, because seeing the gap is clearer than a number. The workbook itself says so on its savings goal visualization page. Turning a guide's example into jars, a range band or a ladder makes an abstract method concrete.
archetypes.layout: Top 0-300: headline. 300-1150: the measuring prop full width: a row of 3-5 sinking-fund-jars on a shelf line, or one range-gauge drawn large with the low and high written under it, or a payoff-ladder beside a small phone-screenshot of the debt screen, or a countdown-strip. Labels sit directly under each object. 1170-1320: sub line. 1360-1460: product line.
archetypes.visual: Labelled jars filled to real proportions, a variable bill as a low-to-high range, the workbook's payoff ladder, the typical-month bar, a 14-day heads-up strip.
archetypes.text: All figures are the guides' own worked examples (sinking-funds-explained, budget-for-variable-bills, 50-30-20-rule-where-it-breaks, subscription-tracker-what-to-track) or the workbook's own labels (payoff ladder p38). No figure is made up for the drawing.
archetypes.bestFor: sinking funds, annual costs, variable bills, 50/30/20, debt payoff, typical month, renewal heads-up
